items.d: From Qazvin you can do a day trip to the mountains of Alborz. Most visitors go here to see the remains of Hasan-e-Sabah's castle Alamut, from where he ruled the assassins order, a medieval terrorist organisation.
The ruined Buddhas are the main reason that most people visit Bamiyan. Although some feel that to visit at all is to reward cultural vandalism and desecration...
The ruins of the Gallo-Roman settlement in Cimiez, plus a museum with nice documentation on Gallo-Roman life (but mostly not in English). Activities for children. Guided tours available.
This is kind of a diminutive mosque compared to some of the great ones out there, but may still be of interest. It is close to the Agbogbloshie borough though, so try not to get lost.
Scenic viewpoint along Jhelum River.
A large spring-fed pool owned by the Pousada, set in lush grounds, with a diving board and a slide. Beautiful place for a swim.
A modern art museum (temporary exhibitions).
Ridiculously over sized and out of place, the palace is one of the best examples of the former dictator's hubris. Situated on a hill overlooking the archaeological site, it provides excellent views.

This is the largest museum collection of foreign art in Serbia. In 1966, Doctor Branko Ilić donated his art collection of 136 paintings of foreign artists, 279 pieces and sculptures, period furniture and other items of applied…
The House of Venus, towards the eastern side of the city under a prominent cypress tree, was one of the most luxurious residences in the city.
The museum is the house of birth of the writer Robert Musil. If you are interested in literature, this is the place to go.
Aka Backside Beach. The beach directly behind the Jesus statue, it's a scenic, inverted c-shaped coastline with near-transparent waters much better than the one at Areia Branca.
This Roman Catholic cathedral is one of the biggest wooden structures on the entire American continent. Building started in 1883 and the church was consecrated two years later.

Built on the site of the former city fortifications, this star-shaped park is the oldest public garden in Germany. It features scenic walking paths, colorful flowerbeds, and the historic "Am Wall" windmill.
Changing contemporary art exhibitions, see website for schedule.

A single-arch stone bridge crosses the Gradeška River, forming quite a picturesque scene. A bridge has existed at this spot for centuries, but it was wooden until the 1950s, when it collapsed as a herd of oxen were crossing.
The main fortress of the ancient town of Mtskheta was located at the high point above the river in strategically good position.
It is a park encompassing the Viroi Lake and surrounding hills. The park features a relaxing environment and an accommodation area.
Regional history museum.

It is the meeting place for the Masonic Lodges. It was built in 1901 during British rule and designed by E. Skinner, an associate of the Royal Institute of British Architects, and built by the Colombo Commercial Company.
Has toilets and showers, some shade and barbeque pits, and is completely surrounded by fencing. The water is shallow with sharp rocks; water shoes recommended.

A volunteer-run charity caring for a large collection of historic buses, coaches and commercial vehicles in a working bus garage. Many of the vehicles still run, and on open days visitors can board them and take short rides.
The Sentiero degli Dei (Path of the Gods) is a spectacular hiking trail along the Amalfi Coast, offering panoramic views of the sea, cliffs, and villages below.
The 43-metre (141 ft) bungy jump off the Kawarau Suspension Bridge is the world's oldest commercial bungy jump, and the only bungy jump in Queenstown offering tandem jumps.

Tour operator offering guided excursions to the Perito Moreno glacier. Specializes in ice trekking (Minitrekking and Big Ice), boat glacier tours (Safari Azul), and kayak expeditions on Lago Argentino.

An important Celtic-Iberian era castro archaeological site with iron age roots. On the EN309 road, not far from Requeixo, this proto-urban site provides an insight into an indigenous people's way of life before being disrupted by…
A must for the visitor. Has some amazing examples of PNG wildlife such as birds of paradise, a couple of casowaris, and several other native birds.
It is also known as Gyeonggi English Village Ansan Camp.
Long tree covered walkway that stretches the city-side banks of the Songhua river, a really nice and pleasant walk.

Grandiose neo-classical building of 1928. Primarily a commercial bank, it has a small exhibition of Lithuanian banknotes and coins of the First Republic, and occasionally hosts larger art installations.
This stretches west of town along the south river bank, with cycling trails and fishing spots. Dogs welcome.

The little St Ann's church is generally mentioned with its neighbouring building, Hungarian Hospital, because the church was built for its residents. The Hospital was founded by the great patron, György Széchenyi in 1666.

n.en: Saint Anne Roman Catholic Church, the former Hungarians ispita

items.d: The gallery at the VCU-Q campus in Education City regularly hosts visiting exhibitions and the work of faculty members and students. On those occasions, the gallery is open to the general public.
The view of the highest mountains north and south of the lake, which can rise above the clouds.
Waterfall on the Miti River, where nationalists were reportedly thrown to their deaths during colonial times and where sacrifices are made to ward off curses, etc. The water falls 40-50 m.

An area with interesting shops and most importantly, a series of residential buildings called "les Schtroumpfs" (1982-1984), where the architects tried to avoid all straight lines, leading to an unconventional Gaudi-like…
Tomb for much loved country freedom fighter.
An Australian Space Agency space discovery centre, opened about the time when Australia joined the space race.
A hexagonal building built on Sagiike Pond in Nara Park so that it appears to float on water.

The historic covered Ottoman market is in the center of the city on the right bank of the Otinja. It was built of stone in the 16th or 17th century. It was destroyed by a fire during the Austro-Turkish war and rebuilt.
